name: Item research
headline: Weekly discovery digest — 6 candidates above affinity threshold

data.pinnedSub: 3 durable · 3 fads · 4 makeable by existing suppliers

__raw.name: Carbon steel wok 12"
__raw.summary: A hand-hammered carbon steel wok sized for home ranges. Sits directly beside our best-selling skillet line, uses the same seasoning story, and needs no new supplier relationship or tooling.

evidence.text: Nine consecutive quarters of search growth with no single-quarter spike above 12% — the shape of adoption, not a viral moment.
Growth is spread across search, marketplace bestseller rank and retail assortment. Fads move on one surface at a time.
Two national brands added a wok SKU in the last 18 months and both are still ranging it — competitor persistence is part of the durability read.

affinityRows: Of orders containing either item, 31% contain both.
Buyers of our carbon steel line index high on wok searches.
Same seasoning and care narrative we already publish.

risks.label: No IP exposure
risks.detail: Commodity form factor, no design patents in the category worth navigating.

risks.label: Mild seasonality
risks.detail: Q4 indexes 1.4× the annual average. Manageable — the same shape as the skillet.

risks.label: Shipping profile
risks.detail: Dim weight is favourable but the 12" diameter needs a new box size — $0.4K of die cost.

supplier.name: Kessler Metalworks (K)
supplier.scope: carbon steel pans, griddles · Tier 1 · 31% of spend
supplier.note: Kessler already presses this gauge on the griddle line. The one open question is hammering finish consistency, which is exactly what the first sample round tests.

__raw.name: Enamel roasting dish set
__raw.summary: Two-piece enamel roasting set in our existing colourway. Arcadia can make it but needs a new mould, which puts $4.2K of tooling deposit inside the sample cost.

evidence.text: Steady 4–5% quarterly growth for three years. Enamel bakeware behaves like a category, not a moment.
Review counts on the top three competitor SKUs are still compounding, which means the category is acquiring buyers rather than recycling them.
Four new entrants in nine months. Durable but crowding — the window for a differentiated entry is narrowing.

affinityRows: Strong pairing with the enamel line we already sell.
Same buyer, same colour preferences, same care instructions.
Colourway and photography style already established.

risks.label: Tooling commitment
risks.detail: A new mould means $4.2K non-refundable before the first sample exists.

risks.label: Crowding
risks.detail: Four entrants in nine months. Differentiation has to come from the colourway, not the form.

risks.label: No IP exposure
risks.detail: Standard roasting form. Nothing to navigate.

supplier.name: Arcadia Enamelworks (A)
supplier.scope: enamel cast iron · Tier 1 · 24% of spend
supplier.note: Arcadia is our best-performing supplier on every standard, which lowers the execution risk. The mould is the cost of admission and it is not recoverable if we park the concept later.

__raw.name: Whetstone angle guide
__raw.summary: A simple machined angle guide for the whetstone we already sell. Cheapest concept on the list to sample, highest margin, smallest revenue ceiling.

evidence.text: Flat, dependable 3% quarterly growth for three years. Accessories to a durable category inherit its durability.
Our own whetstone buyers search for angle guides at 4.1× the site average — this is demand we are currently sending elsewhere.
Small addressable revenue: modelled at $34K a year. High margin, low ceiling — an attachment, not a hero.

affinityRows: Nearly half of whetstone orders would plausibly attach.
Narrower audience than the knife line itself.
Slots into the sharpening guide we already publish.

risks.label: Low revenue ceiling
risks.detail: Modelled at $34K a year. Worth doing, not worth prioritising over a hero.

risks.label: No IP exposure
risks.detail: Simple machined form, widely produced.

risks.label: No seasonality
risks.detail: Flat demand across the year, which makes it easy to plan.

supplier.name: Tsuyo Blades (T)
supplier.note: Tsuyo has the fastest sampling turnaround of any supplier and meets every performance standard. The only conversation open with them is payment terms, which is separate from this.

__raw.name: Silicone lid-and-strainer combo
__raw.summary: Currently spiking on short-form video. No existing supplier makes silicone, the durability read is poor, and the projected margin is below our floor before tooling.

evidence.text: Search volume rose 141% in one quarter and has fallen for three consecutive quarters since. Classic single-platform spike.
84% of the signal traces to a single short-video format. Marketplace bestseller rank never followed the search spike.
Two competitors who ranged it in the spike have already delisted. That is the strongest fad evidence available.

affinityRows: Weak attachment to anything we currently sell.
Younger than our base, which is why affinity scored above 70.
Reads as novelty against a durable-goods brand.

risks.label: Fad classification
risks.detail: Durability 31% ± 14. The spike has already decayed three quarters running.

risks.label: No supplier capability
risks.detail: None of our four suppliers work silicone. A new relationship is a separate decision with its own cost.

risks.label: Brand fit
risks.detail: Single-purpose gadget. Fails the durable-and-repairable constraint set in Reason.

supplier.name: No existing supplier
supplier.scope: silicone moulding — outside all four suppliers’ capability
supplier.note: Sourcing this means onboarding a supplier for a product the classifier says will not exist as a category in eighteen months. The preferred-supplier constraint from Reason rules it out on its own.

__raw.name: Countertop compost caddy
__raw.summary: Enamel compost caddy riding a municipal-composting rollout. Real demand, geographically concentrated, and the durability read is dominated by regulation rather than taste.

evidence.text: Growth traces to three metro composting mandates. Real, but the curve has flattened and turned down as rollout completed.
Demand is concentrated in four states. National ranging would carry inventory in markets with no mandate.
Two further metros have mandates scheduled for next year — the revisit trigger writes itself.

affinityRows: Almost no attachment to our current range.
Same buyer as our enamel line, which is why it scored.
Enamel and durability fit; the use case does not.

risks.label: Regulation-dependent demand
risks.detail: The curve follows mandates, not preference. Durability 42% ± 16.

risks.label: Geographic concentration
risks.detail: Four states carry the demand. National inventory would sit.

risks.label: Margin below target
risks.detail: 41% against a 42% floor before any tooling amortisation.

supplier.name: Arcadia Enamelworks (A)
supplier.scope: enamel cast iron · Tier 1 · 24% of spend
supplier.note: Arcadia can make it well. The question is not capability — it is whether we want $3.6K of non-recoverable tooling against a demand curve that has already turned.

__raw.name: Magnetic knife rail 18"
__raw.summary: Steel magnetic rail with strong adjacency to our knife line. The economics work; the trend read is weak and three competitors are already deep in the category.

evidence.text: Peaked six quarters ago and has declined every quarter since. Growth is behind it, not ahead.
Three established brands hold 71% of marketplace share with review counts we could not match inside two years.
The one genuine positive: 44% CM and strong basket logic with the knife line. Good economics on a shrinking category.

affinityRows: Same buyer as the knife line.
Fits the kitchen but adds nothing to the story.

risks.label: Declining category
risks.detail: Six quarters of decline. Durability 38% ± 12.

risks.label: Entrenched competition
risks.detail: Three brands hold 71% share with review moats we cannot cross quickly.

risks.label: Shipping and damage
risks.detail: 18" length pushes into oversize on two channels; magnets need careful packing.

supplier.name: Kessler Metalworks (K)
supplier.scope: carbon steel pans, griddles · Tier 1 · 31% of spend
supplier.note: Kessler is mid-negotiation on a price increase, which is not a reason to avoid them but is a reason not to add a new tooling commitment this month.
